message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—on the order of **\(10^{43}\)**.  

This figure comes from combinatorial estimates that take into account all the ways pieces can be arranged on the board while respecting the rules of movement, castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, and pawn promotion choices. It’s often called the “Shannon number” for legal positions. 

For comparison, the total number of possible games of chess (including all move sequences) is even larger, roughly \(10^{120}\).
